schema_version: v0 — migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: Session-continuity records — the state of work at a session boundary, so the next session resumes without re-deriving.
why: Sessions are bounded by context limits; continuity must live in a durable, shareable artifact, not in memory of a conversation that won't survive the boundary. A slate is knowledge the SYSTEM would lose (not just CC's personal memory). Written by skill:/saveslate, read by cairn/bin/cmd/slate — a PROGRAM fired by a SessionStart hook, not a skill, since 2026-07-31. That asymmetry is deliberate and load-bearing: finding the newest record and printing three ratified fields is settled and compiles (Law 1); deciding what the session's state WAS is judgment and does not. The consequence for this store is that its records are now read unconditionally at every session open, so a slate's length is a standing context cost rather than an optional one.
owner: the slates store owns writes; the single commons emit chokepoint validates every record against the template below (Law 6).

template.written_at: ISO-8601 absolute instant the door wrote this record — the rank key WITHIN a date (added 2026-08-03; records written before it carry none)
template.author: who wrote it (CC | Akien)
template.at_sea: what is actively being worked, and its state
template.open_threads: array — unresolved questions, IOUs, things to verify (each honest about my-read vs ratified)

notes_on_the_store: A slate is a best-guess snapshot at a boundary, carrying its open threads — not a claim anything is finished (learning-loop keystone).
The map (MAP.md) is authoritative over memory of the conversation; a slate is authoritative for session continuity. Drift between them is named, not silently reconciled.
A slate that names a file/flag/ticket is a pointer to verify (Law 3), not a proof.

THE DAY IS NOT THE RANK (2026-08-03). 'Newest' was date + filename, and filenames tiebreak alphabetically on the TITLE, which carries no time. Three slates were written on 2026-08-03; the 15:50 one outranked the 16:41 one, so that session open presented a slate one voyage behind as ground truth and the next session did not know /challenge had shipped. mtime is still refused as the fix (14 slates were bulk-touched once, and that is why this ranking reads the records' own fields). The door already held the write instant and was discarding it at day granularity — it now stamps written_at. Records predating the stamp carry none and rank BELOW any stamped record of the same day; a day of only-unstamped records still falls back to filename order and the reader SAYS so rather than presenting a guess as the answer.

READ IS AUTOMATIC, WRITE IS NOT (2026-07-31). The reader consumes a CLOSED SET — at_sea, next_direction, open_threads — and deliberately ignores any other key, so a slate that grows a field (two have: 'continues', 'how_this_session_went', 'the_sweep_in_one_line') is not read wider without a change here first. The store charter is the gate on what a session sees, which is where that decision belongs.
